chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever consoles a bereaved person, he will have the like of his reward, without anything being reduced from the reward of the bereaved.'

key_terms.مُصَاباً: a bereaved person / one struck by calamity

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for consoling a grieving person according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith underscores the communal nature of grief in Shia ethics, where consoling the bereaved yields a reward equal to their own without any diminution. This principle highlights the spiritual economy of compassion, encouraging believers to actively participate in alleviating others' sorrow as a means of shared spiritual elevation.
